title: Threat Models: Assets, Attackers, and Trust Boundaries Check

questions.prompt: Which design best applies threat models: assets, attackers, and trust boundaries?
options: Model the transfer asset, actors, data flows, trust boundaries, abuse paths, controls, and residual risk before selecting APIs.
Encrypt every String in the app
Assume the app sandbox removes all threats
questions.answer: Model the transfer asset, actors, data flows, trust boundaries, abuse paths, controls, and residual risk before selecting APIs.
questions.explanation: The strongest option enforces authority at the correct boundary and includes limitations, lifecycle, adversarial verification, and recovery.

questions.prompt: A trust boundary exists only where traffic crosses the public internet.
questions.explanation: Starting with a checklist of APIs before identifying assets and attack paths can harden irrelevant code while the real authority boundary remains exposed.

questions.prompt: What makes a threat scenario actionable?
questions.answer: It names an asset, attacker capability, boundary, abuse path, impact, control, evidence, owner, and residual risk.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the specific security property and boundary required by the lesson rather than naming a library.
